title: Improving field phenotyping accuracy in rice: a comparative study of smartphone image analysis and manual measurement
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) production is threatened by bacterial leaf blight (BLB), particularly from the virulent K3a strain. Reliableand efficient phenotyping is essential for breeding resistant cultivars, but traditional manual methods are time-consuming and prone to subjectivity. This study assessed the accuracy of smartphone-based image analysis for measuring lesion length (LL) and lesion ratio (LR) in BLB-infectedrice. A total of 102 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) derived from Chamdongjin and Sindongjin were evaluated using both manual methods and imageanalysis. Images were captured in the field using a smartphone (12MP, 4000×3000 pixels), without any auxiliary equipment. The images were analyzedusing ImageJ and Python-based tools and compared with manual measurements. Image-based data showed strong correlation with manual results(r = 0.84–1.00), and principal component analysis (PCA) explained 94.14% of the variance, effectively distinguishing resistant and susceptible lines.Statistically significant differences were observed between groups (p < 0.01), confirming reliability. Images taken at 3x magnification showed highaccuracy (r = 0.88–0.92), while those at 1x magnification showed reduced accuracy (r = 0.76–0.79), likely due to the inclusion of surrounding plants—highlighting the importance of proper field design and image framing. This study suggests that smartphone-acquired images, even withoutauxiliary equipment, may serve as a feasible and sufficiently accurate source for image-based phenotyping. This accessible approach has the potential tosupport rapid, low-cost data collection in field settings, which could contribute to breeding and disease resistance research. Smartphone-based image measurements were strongly correlated with conventional measurements of rice bacterial leaf blight symptoms. Images captured at3×magnification showed stronger correlations with reference measurements than images captured at 1×magnification. Lesion ratio showed greaterconsistency across ImageJ and Python analyses than lesion length. Smartphone-based field imaging distinguished resistant and susceptible rice lineswithout additional imaging equipment.

title: Correction to: MS-R outperforms RGB: Lightweight CYOLO-BiCNet enables efficient detection and storage optimization of cotton flowers
3D modeling for crop applications in precision agriculture: a review
abstract: Background Advances in data acquisition and information processing have strengthened the role of precision agriculture (PA) in enhancing agricultural productivity and sustainability. Among emerging technologies, 3D crop modeling offers detailed representations of agricultural scenes, supports crop phenotyping, and enables autonomous operations such as harvesting, fertilization, and pruning. However, despite the rapid development of hardware and software for 3D modeling, a comprehensive synthesis of the available approaches and their applications in PA remains limited. Purpose This review aims to examine the broad range of 3D modeling approaches used in PA, focusing on their methodological characteristics, practical applications, advantages, and limitations to support the selection of suitable solutions for different agricultural requirements. Methods A total of 168 publications, identified through a Scopus literature search covering studies published up to March 2026, were reviewed. The analysis examines 3D data types and sensing technologies, sensor platforms and application environments, and data processing methods, including data registration techniques and methods for insight extraction. Applications of 3D models to agricultural crops were also analyzed and classified into three main categories: crop phenotyping, machinery navigation, and field operations. Conclusions The review highlights the widespread adoption of LiDAR, RGB, and RGB-D sensors deployed on Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles, Uncrewed Ground Vehicles, and robotic platforms, alongside increasing use of AI-based processing methods. Challenges related to sensor robustness, multisensor interoperability, and large 3D datasets remain. Future research should focus on overcoming these limitations to facilitate the transition towards reliable, large-scale implementation of 3D modeling technologies in practical agricultural operations.

title: Reconstruction of within-field spatio-temporal variability from fixed and on-board proximal sensors: application to simulated leaf area data in viticulture
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the reconstruction of spatio-temporal variability in vineyards by combining data from fixed and mobile sensors: fixed sensors monitor temporal changes on a few specific plants, while mobile sensors collect spatial data at specific times. It focuses on the Leaf Area Index (LAI) as a key indicator of crop development that can be measured on almost any plant at any time. Methods The methodology involves the simulation of LAI data from April to October, taking into account phenological, environmental and plant variability, as well as sensor errors. Data fusion methods, spatio-temporal inverse distance weighting (STIDW), spatio-temporal kriging (STK) and generalized additive models (GAM), were evaluated to reconstruct LAI dynamics from available sensor data. Results Although these three methods all gave satisfactory results with reconstruction error not higher than \(10\%\) , STK and GAM performed better than STIDW in reconstructing spatial structure. However, GAM showed flexibility in modelling non-linear relationships and outperformed other models in the case of a more heterogeneous plot. Different sampling scenarios showed that increasing the number of spatial maps and fixed sensors improved the reconstruction by about \(5\%\) , with spatial maps having a greater impact. Conclusion The spatio-temporal variability of the vineyard can be reconstructed with a limited number of fixed sensors and monthly acquisitions with mobile sensors at the beginning of the season, for example 4 monthly acquisitions from April to July and from 3 to 8 fixed sensors per hectare depending on the complexity of the plot. This study highlights the benefits of data fusion to improve precision farming applications.

title: Barley head detection using UAV imagery and YOLOv10
abstract: Abstract Barley head detection is a crucial task for agricultural applications such as yield estimation and crop monitoring. Unlike wheat, automated barley head detection has not been extensively studied due to challenges posed by its complex head structures and the lack of annotated datasets. In this paper, we leverage YOLOv10, a state-of-the-art object detection framework, to detect barley heads from high-resolution images captured using UAVs. Our dataset, consisting of UAV-captured images and supplemented with the Global Wheat Head Dataset, provides a robust foundation for model training. The proposed approach achieves a mean Average Precision of 0.83 at Intersection of Union 0.5, setting a new benchmark for barley head detection. This work contributes to advancing automated crop monitoring systems in precision agriculture.

title: AutoPlot grid: development and quantitative evaluation of an RTK-GNSS-based tool for automated breeding-plot delineation and UAV phenotyping data extraction
abstract: Purpose: Plant breeders use unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to collect multispectral (MS) imagery for field-based phenotyping; however, plotlevel analysis remains limited by the time and user intervention required to delineate plot boundaries and extract phenotyping data across large breedingtrials. This study aimed to develop and quantitatively evaluate an automated workflow that integrates planter-recorded real-time kinematic global navigation satellite system (RTK-GNSS) data with UAV MS imagery for breeding-plot delineation and phenotyping-data extraction. Methods: Plot boundaries were generated from planter RTK-GNSS points grouped using HDBSCAN, with a generalized plot-offset formulation supporting flexible rowsper-plot configurations and unique plot identification. The workflow integrated batch vegetation index (VI) calculation and zonal-statistics extraction within a graphical user interface. Automated boundaries were evaluated against expert manually delineated polygons for 1,360 two-row soybean plotsusing centroid displacement, orientation, dimensions, intersection-over-union (IoU), and VI agreement. Processing time was compared with manual andgrid-based ArcGIS Pro workflows by two users. Results: Mean centroid displacement was 17.62 cm (RMSE 18.89 cm), orientation differences were negligible, and mean IoU was 0.778. Approximately 99.63% of plots were within 38 cm, one-half of the 0.76-m row spacing. NDVI, NDRE, and GNDVIshowed Pearson correlations greater than 0.90 with manual extraction. Processing time was reduced by 94.2–95.5% relative to manual polygon drawing and by 83.5–87.0% relative to grid-based ArcGIS Pro processing. Conclusion: Planter RTK-GNSS data can provide a consistent and scalable spatial reference for automated breeding-plot delineation and canopy-focused UAV phenotyping, while preserving plot-level VI patterns and substantially reducing manual processing effort.

title: A growing challenge: stakeholder perceptions of AI and ML applications in U.S. agriculture
abstract: Abstract Context The global population is expected to exceed ten billion by 2050 and food demand is projected to increase by up to 100% in the same timeframe. Agricultural management must adapt to meet the increasing global demands. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies can help the agricultural community respond to these needs. Aims An online survey and follow-up interviews were conducted to examine patterns of use, perceptions, and barriers among early adopting stakeholders regarding AI and ML. Methods The online survey with agricultural stakeholders (n=129) included questions regarding the participants’ views on incorporating AI and ML techniques into farming practices and individual follow-up interviews with agricultural stakeholders (n=10) were conducted to better understand their concerns toward technology use and adoption of AI-enabled tools and technologies. Key results Using a mixed-methods approach, four challenges to establishing AI-/ML-enabled technology in agriculture were identified. Namely, challenges related to (1) systems of systems (SoS), (2) sub-seasonal to seasonal weather (S2S) forecasts, (3) precision soil management, and (4) policy and economics. Each challenge was discussed in the context of recent literature. Conclusion Concerns were voiced clustered around four broad research themes. This brief communication brings the perspective of agricultural stakeholders to the discussion of the potential of AI/ML-enabled technology and the direction of their development in the agricultural sector. Implications Data collected in 2021, establish an important baseline for the early phase of AI/ML use in U.S. agriculture, enabling comparison of future perceptions and developments in the sector. Impact This brief communication describes a survey and follow-up interviews conducted with agricultural stakeholders on factors influencing their willingness and reluctance to incorporate AI and ML techniques into farming practices. The findings, summarized and discussed as four key challenges for AI and ML in the agricultural sector, have the potential to streamline research activities.

title: Enhancing seeding efficiency using a computer vision system to monitor furrow quality in real-time
abstract: Purpose Crop residue interference (hair-pinning) poses a critical barrier to optimal seed furrow formation in conservation tillage, yet currentmanual assessments prevent real-time equipment optimization. The purpose of this study was to develop a high-speed computer vision (CV) methodology to answer the following research question: Can real-time semantic segmentation dynamically quantify seed trench cleanliness and evaluate row cleanerperformance accurately enough to enable autonomous seeding adjustments and eliminate labor-intensive manual assessments? Methods A high-definitionvideo acquisition system was integrated onto an air seeder. The study benchmarked five semantic segmentation architectures (SegFormer, DeepLabV3+,PSPNet, U-Net, and K-Net) to identify a model capable of balancing segmentation accuracy with the strict latency constraints of high-speed planting. Thismethodology was subsequently applied as a proof-of-concept to test four prototype pre-production row cleaner configurations. Results The TransformerbasedSegFormer emerged as the optimal architecture, achieving an 80.9% Soil Intersection over Union (IoU) with an exceptionally fast inference time of11.75 ms. When applied to the row cleaner prototypes, the system revealed that the optimal configuration increased soil exposure to 80.3%, compared to abaseline operation that retained 61.1% residue cover. Conclusion Real-time semantic segmentation via this CV system effectively resolves the complexvisual challenges of furrow analysis. By proving its viability for real-time deployment, this methodology provides a foundational perception layer crucialfor the future of autonomous seeding equipment.

title: Robust and transparent crop-row detection from RGB field imagery for vision-based agricultural guidance systems
abstract: Purpose Robust crop-row detection from field imagery is an important perception capability for agricultural guidance and robotic systems operating under variable field conditions. However, many existing approaches rely on strong geometric assumptions, specific crop configurations, or large annotated datasets. Methods This study proposes a transparent deterministic image-processing framework for automatic crop-row detection in RGB imagery. The method progressively extracts vegetation structures, analyses their spatial organization, reconstructs directional gaps, and derives crop-row geometry through centroid-based guidance, skeletonization, polynomial modelling, line connection, and extension. The framework does not require prior knowledge of row number, row spacing, planting geometry, camera calibration, or crop identity. Results Experiments were conducted using 1,373 manually annotated images covering multiple crops and field conditions. On a common 150-image held-out test set, the proposed method yielded the lowest point estimates for row-count MAE (2.3 rows), lateral MAE (8.9 pixels), and RMSE (10.4 pixels), and the highest Precision (95.3%), Recall (93.7%), and F1-score (94.3%) among the evaluated approaches. Paired statistical analysis showed that these differences were not uniformly supported across all reference methods and metrics. An incremental ablation analysis further supported the contribution of the terminal structural-refinement stages. Conclusion The proposed framework provides a transparent, weak-prior approach to crop-row reconstruction without crop-specific training. Its consistent performance across the evaluated scenarios supports further investigation as a perception component for agricultural guidance systems, while independent external and operational validation remains necessary.

title: UAV-based multispectral imaging and machine learning for characterizing herbicide injury and desiccant responses in field crops
abstract: Abstract Purpose Herbicides and desiccants are critical for weed control and harvest management; however, their efficacy varies across crop species, environments, and growing seasons. This study evaluated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral imaging combined with machine-learning (ML) as a non-destructive approach for quantifying herbicide injury and desiccation responses across Canadian Prairie agroecosystems. Methods Field trials were conducted from 2022 to 2024 at three sites in Alberta and Saskatchewanusing tame oat, oriental mustard, and lentil. Tame oat and oriental mustard were used as pseudo-weed models for wild oat and wild mustard, respectively. UAV multispectral imagery and concurrent ground-based visual ratings were collected from 0 to 21 days aftertreatment to characterize temporal crop responses. Six ML models were evaluated using UAV-derived vegetation indices. Results Ensemble models, including Gradient Boosting, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest, consistently demonstrated strong predictive performance, with site-specific coefficients of determination (R) of 66–90% in oat, 60–75% in mustard, and 43–96% in lentil. Multi-site models achieved R values of 65–83%; however, leave-one-site-out (LOSO) and leave-one-year-out (LOYO) validation for oat and mustard showed reduced predictive performance in independent environments, highlighting limitations in model transferability. Vegetation indices captured temporal herbicide injury and stress dynamics across crops, while area under the desiccation progress curve (AUDPC) analysis quantified lentil dry-down and differentiated desiccant performance. Pearson correlation analysis identified NDVI and NDGI indices strongly associated with visual injury ratings across crops and environments. NDVI showed the most consistent relationships in oat and mustard, whereas NDVI, NDGI, and VARI exhibited comparable relationships with lentil desiccation responses. Conclusion Overall, integrating UAV-based multispectral imaging, vegetation indices, ML, and AUDPC provides a scalable, objective, and non-destructive framework for evaluating herbicide injury and desiccant efficacy under variable field conditions.

title: Precision maize crop height mapping using multispectral and LiDAR data from unmanned aerial system
abstract: Abstract Context Spatially explicit and accurate maize crop height maps are essential for supporting site-specific management in precision agriculture. Although low-cost unmanned aerial system (UAS)-based multispectral imagery offers a promising approach for maize crop height estimation, it’s accuracy under varying canopy conditions remains uncertain. Aims In this study, we used 3D point clouds to estimate maize crop height during sparse and dense canopy cover based on UAS-captured multispectral images and compare with light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based estimates. Methods The 3D point clouds from multispectral images and LiDAR data were processed using a spatially localized grid (SLG) filtering approachto derive digital terrain model (DTM) and canopy surface model (CSM), which were then used to estimate maize crop height.Furthermore, two strategies were explored — (1) grid expansion, and (2) using ground reference derived during sparse canopy aspotential tools to mitigate issues during dense canopy cover for multispectral image-based estimations. Results Results showed that the crop height estimated from multispectral images during sparse canopy cover show comparable accuracy (r = 0.9, nRMSE = 32%) to LiDAR-based estimation (r = 0.81, nRMSE = 17%). The accuracy of multispectral-based estimation, however, significantly declined under dense canopy cover, where no meaningful correlation was observed (r = − 0.1, nRMSE = 61%). In contrast, LiDAR-based estimates show consistent level of accuracy under the same conditions (r = 0.78, nRMSE = 15%). When grid expansion strategy was implemented for multispectral-based estimation during the dense canopy cover, the nRMSE was observed to decrease up to 28%. Meanwhile, with the use of sparse canopy cover ground reference, the nRMSE decreased up to 17%, comparable to the LiDAR-based estimate. Conclusion Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of deriving crop heights cost-effectively using multispectral imaging from UAS. This approach offers a scalable and economically viable alternative to expensive LiDAR systems, enabling wider integration of crop height information into precision agriculture applications.

title: Using shortwave infrared spectral indices to monitor short-term water stress dynamics in peach orchards
abstract: Abstract Purpose Capturing rapid changes in water status is key to optimizing deficit irrigation in Mediterranean orchards, but thermal remote sensing is constrained by the availability of high-spatial-resolution data. This study assesses the ability of visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared (VNIR/SWIR) indices to detect short-term water stress in peach orchards. Methods An experiment was conducted in two commercial orchards in south-eastern Spain, where mild water stress was induced by withholding irrigation for four days. High-resolution hyperspectral and thermal imagery were acquired concurrently with stem water potential measurements (ψ stem ). Structural, pigment-related, and water-sensitive indices were evaluated at several spatial resolutions, from high (20–50 cm) to medium (30 m), to analyze the effects of pixel size on stress detection. The Crop Water Stress Index (CWSI), derived from thermal imagery, served as a reference indicator. Results Those optical indices based on SWIR reflectance at 1240 nm, the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI₁₂₄₀) and the Simple Ratio Water Index (SRWI), showed the strongest sensitivity to ψ stem variability (R 2 = 0.63, p < 0.001), comparable to the thermal CWSI (R 2 = 0.67, p < 0.001). The analyzed SWIR indices proved more robust under spatial aggregation than other classical VNIR indices, preserving sensitivity when soil/shadow effects were included. Radiative transfer simulations (PROSPECT/3D FLIGHT model) confirmed the NDWI₁₂₄₀ response to variations in leaf water content and leaf angle under short-term stress. Conclusion The results demonstrate the potential of SWIR-based indices, especially in the 1200–1300 nm range, to detect early water stress in Mediterranean woody crops and support their applicability for large-scale monitoring with current and upcoming satellite sensors, though further validation using operational satellite data is required.

title: Development and evaluation of an on-the-go variable rate nitrogen application algorithm for open-field Borettana onion (Allium cepa L.) cultivation
abstract: Purpose Efficient nitrogen (N) management is crucial for maximizing growth, bulb yield, and nutrient use efficiency in high-value horticultural crops, such as Borettana onion ( Allium cepa L.). However, excessive or poorly timed N applications can reduce fertilizer use efficiency and increase the risk of environmental losses. This study aimed to develop and validate a growth-stage adaptive, N variable-rate application (N-VRA) strategy for Borettana onion under open-field conditions. Methods The approach combined biomass estimation based on thermal time (growing degree days, GDD), determination of critical N requirements, and real-time crop monitoring through NDVI measurements. Four-year field trials conducted in northeastern Italy employed fixed-rate N applications (150–240 kg N ha⁻ 1 ) during 2021–2022 to develop the N-VRA algorithm, followed by 2023–2024 trials for testing and validation. Trials were arranged in randomized complete block designs with four to five replications per treatment on large plots (48 × 50 m to 48 × 74 m in size) Results Results showed that thermal time was able to accurately predict the growing biomass (R 2 = 0.98; RMSE = 1.2 t ha⁻ 1 ); meanwhile, the critical N dilution curve effectively captured the relationship between biomass and optimal N concentration (R 2 = 0.81; RMSE = 0.30%). In addition, NDVI-based assessments enabled real-time, growth stage-specific adjustments of N supply according to crop demand, thereby demonstrating a strong predictive relationship with crop N status. Compared with conventional methods, N-VRA maintained high standards of onion yield, significantly improved the proportion of marketable bulbs by up to 28%, and significantly enhanced N use efficiency by up to 36%, while reducing total N inputs. Conclusion This integrated, site-specific framework offers a practical and environmentally sustainable strategy for precision N management in Borettana onion production.

title: Vegetation index-based hyperspectral assessment of sequential herbicide combinations on maize physiology and weed response under controlled maize–weed system
abstract: Purpose Conventional visual evaluation methods often fail to detect herbicide-induced physiological responses during the initial post-application period, limiting the early assessment of herbicide efficacy for precision weed management. Therefore, this study investigated the potential of vegetation index-based hyperspectral phenotyping, combined with multivariate and machine-learning approaches, for the rapid diagnosis of the effectiveness of sequential herbicide programs in a maize-weed system. Methods A controlled pot experiment was conducted using four sequential herbicide programs comprising pyroxasulfone fb halosulfuron methyl, pyroxasulfone fb tembotrione, atrazine fb halosulfuron methyl and atrazine fb tembotrione, along with an untreated weedy control. Visible-near infrared (VNIR; 400–1000 nm) hyperspectral imagery was acquired before post emergence herbicide application and at 2, 4, 6, and 9 days after application (DAA). Multiple vegetation indices representing chlorophyll status, canopy structure, pigment composition, stress responses, and water status were derived from hyperspectral reflectance data. Principal component analysis (PCA), correlation analysis, hierarchical clustering, and supervised classification models (logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine) were employed to evaluate treatment discrimination and early diagnostic separability. Results Tembotrione-based treatments, particularly pyroxasulfone (PE) fb tembotrione (PoE), produced the strongest physiological responses, causing pronounced reductions in chlorophyll-, red-edge-, structural-, stress-, and water-related vegetation indices within four days after application. In contrast, halosulfuron methyl-based treatments exhibited spectral trends similar to the untreated control, indicating limited impact on the existing weed flora. Among the evaluated indices, GDVI, GNDVI, NDRE, mNDVI 705 , and mRESR were the most sensitive indicators of early herbicide stress. PCA revealed that the first two principal components explained more than 90% of total variability, clearly separating tembotrione-based treatments from halosulfuron methyl treatments and the weedy check. Hierarchical clustering and correlation analyses further confirmed treatment-specific physiological responses. Supervised classification models successfully classified herbicide treatment-response groups under controlled conditions, with Random Forest achieving the highest performance (ROC-AUC: 0.981 ± 0.020), demonstrating the potential utility of PCA-derived hyperspectral features for treatment-response detection. Conclusion Hyperspectral vegetation indices enabled early, objective detection of herbicide-induced stress before visible symptoms appeared. Chlorophyll- and red-edge-sensitive indices were the most responsive indicators of herbicide activity. The integration of hyperspectral phenomics with multivariate analysis and machine-learning classification provided reliable early discrimination of herbicide efficacy, highlighting its potential as a practical decision-support approach for precision weed management and future sensor-based monitoring systems.
